result.label: feature
result.what_to_change: slugify() strips anything outside [a-z0-9] after NFKD normalization, which removes Greek/Cyrillic letters entirely (they have no Latin decomposition), unlike accented Latin letters which just lose diacritics. Extend slugify (or add an option used by formatExportFilename in src/exportUtils.ts) to preserve non-Latin letters (e.g. keep \p{L}\p{N} characters) instead of discarding anything non-ASCII, so Greek/Cyrillic report names survive into export file names.
result.evidence: src/util/strings.ts: slugify() does value.normalize('NFKD').replace(/[̀-ͯ]/g,'').toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g,'-'), which keeps only ASCII letters/digits -- Greek/Cyrillic characters have no decomposition into those, so they are replaced with '-' and stripped, while formatExportFilename in src/exportUtils.ts falls back to 'report' when slugify returns empty, matching the reported behavior exactly.

could_not_determine: Whether other callers of slugify (e.g. URLs) also need Unicode letters preserved, or only export filenames should change.

text: This confirms the root cause: `slugify` uses NFKD normalization and strips combining marks then restricts to `[a-z0-9]`, dropping any non-Latin characters (Greek, Cyrillic) entirely, resulting in empty base and fallback to "report".

slugify() only keeps ASCII letters/digits after NFKD normalization, so Greek/Cyrillic letters (which have no Latin decomposition) are stripped entirely, unlike accented Latin letters which just lose diacritics. This causes formatExportFilename in src/exportUtils.ts to fall back to 'report' for such names, matching the reported behavior.
